paper_title: The Unseen Targets of Hate -- A Systematic Review of Hateful   Communication Datasets
caption: Monolingual vs. multilingual datasets over time. While monolingual datasets are more frequent, around 2017 researchers began producing multilingual datasets.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the number of datasets related to hateful communication, categorized by language type—monolingual (labeled "1") and multilingual (labeled "2+")—over the years from 2012 to 2022. The vertical axis, labeled "Number of datasets," uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 10 to 100, while the horizontal axis represents the year. Monolingual datasets, represented by blue bars, are consistently more numerous than multilingual datasets, shown by the orange bars, across all years. In 2012 and 2013, the number of datasets is low, with only a few monolingual datasets. From 2014 to 2016, the number of monolingual datasets increases, with a noticeable jump in 2016. The number of monolingual datasets continues to rise sharply, reaching approximately 90 in 2021. Multilingual datasets begin to appear in 2017, with a small number of datasets, and their count increases over time, reaching around 25 in 2021. In 2022, the number of monolingual datasets remains high, while the number of multilingual datasets drops significantly. The chart highlights a growing trend in the production of both types of datasets, with a notable increase in multilingual datasets starting around 2017, as indicated by the caption.
